Status: Wave 322 accepted (6.3): the CoAP transmission manager and the managed stacks' CoapClient

Method.evidence: Class1079 (CoapTransmissionManager, named in wave 319) has 6.4 CoapTransmissionManager's field list in order (receiver, transmitter, coapProcessor_0, coapTransmissionQueue_0, two TimeSpans, bools, a task list, the BufferBlocks and the singleton), so its four free accessors take 6.4's names: get_Receiver and get_Transmitter from plain readonly fields, get_CoapProcessor and get_CoapTransmissionQueue from the auto-property backing fields. Interface45 is the transmitter contract (6.4 ICoapTransmitter) and Class1084 is the queue (6.4 State.CoapTransmissionQueue). The five managed-stack helpers (Class1348 ManagedIoTStack, Class1349, Class1351 IoTGroupCommunicationManagedStackHelper, Class1353 IoTRestManagedStackHelper, Class1360 IoTSecurityManagedStackHelper) each expose the CoapClient through the property 6.4 declares as `public CoapClient CoapClient`.
Method.themes: Closes the CoAP stack's collaborator surface for the transmission manager and the managed stacks. What remains in these classes is either obfuscated in 6.4 too (method_8/11/12/13, method_16/17/18) or compiler-generated accessors (the BufferBlock/CancellationTokenSource/TimeSpan getters, the singleton smethod_0), which need behaviour evidence rather than a counterpart name.
